rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian on two HIGH objections, and THE GATING ONE IS RIGHT. Every objection below is answered with a check, not an argument — the code is committed (e1951c24b) and the migration applied, so these are readings, not promises.

GATING (prior_art_librarian, HIGH, edits 3+4): I described KnownAspectsSorted as 'the guard's OWN function' in edit 3 while edit 4 CREATED it by extraction. That is a real internal contradiction in my wording and the seat was right to refuse on it. The correct statement, checked against the commit's parent rather than asserted (`git show e1951c24b~1:<file> | grep -c 'func <sym>'`): resolveStorageIdentity PRE-EXISTED (component_storage_identity.go:60, unexported but same package `actions`, so callable — and previously called only from store_generated_component_action.go:115, which is exactly why edit 2 is a NEW composition and the seat was right to want that said); LoadKnownSpecAspects PRE-EXISTED (component_source_guard.go:207); KnownQueryBases PRE-EXISTED (queryresolve/queryresolve.go:231, shipped by 0df9f1be9, bugs_open/309's own fix); KnownAspectsSorted did NOT EXIST — I created it in this change by extracting the inline sort+render at component_source_guard.go:188-193, and the point of extracting it is that the refusal message and the advisory then share one rendering. So the honest claim is THREE reused, ONE extracted-to-be-shared — not four reused. Corrected throughout.

GUARDIAN (medium x2 — the most valuable objection in the round, because it names the way this fix could look shipped and deliver nothing): 'if Arm B's destination key is a NEW output_field distinct from existing_component, migration 565's {{if .existing_component.aspect_paths}} guard would never fire.' Checked at the live row, not in the sketch: load_existing_component's step declares `output_field = existing_component`, generate_template's input_fields is [input_data, site_record, site_specs, existing_component], and the Go code merges the vocabulary INTO the same returned map via a withVocabulary closure applied on all five return paths (load_existing_component_action.go:135-141, 183, 192, 200). So there is no new output_field and no new top-level key; the vocabulary rides inside the already-declared existing_component object. This also answers guidelines' medium (the 2026-08-11 nested-field ruling: exempt if nested inside an already-declared object AND named in the register entry in the shipping commit) — it is nested, and CLC-027 is registered with the index row added.

REUSE_AGENT (medium): 'the flagship failing example is a tool page, plausibly served by create_tool_component rather than component-creator, so this may fix one path and leave the other.' Checked both halves. (a) The flagship case is NOT on that path: loanzy.uk's loans-credit-health-check item is item_type=needs_new_component, handled_by=build-dispatch-loop → component-creator → store_generated_component, i.e. the path this change fixes. (b) The seat's broader point is REAL and I had not checked it: create_tool_component_action.go runs NEITHER gate (0 occurrences of SourceVocabularyIssues or schemaFieldSet, against 5 in store_generated_component_action.go). But it is not currently a hole, and the measurement is the useful part: of its 125 active tool-level components, 98 carry a NULL input_schema — they declare no sources for either gate to validate — and the other 27 DO have a fields object and are therefore already covered by the at-rest audit, which reports zero offenders among them. I checked this the careful way round rather than reading the audit's silence as a pass: the audit does not filter on component_level, so the question was whether the rows are invisible to it, and they are invisible only because they declare nothing. Recorded as a contrib in bugs_open/362 as a hole that opens the moment that path emits sources.

BUG_HISTORIAN (medium, edit 3, and the sharpest observation in the round): telling the writer valid aspect names makes the LEAF-KEY miss more reachable, not less — a writer that previously invented 'ctas' (loudly refused) may now confidently construct cta.<plausible key> (silently blank). I had not made that point myself. Two responses. (1) It is now FILED, not prose: a contrib into bugs_open/362 naming it as a residual of that rule, with the reasons a full-path check is architecture-scope (must replicate navigateMap plus both alias chains or over-refuse; per-site truth vs fleet-shared components; a fourth class into a vocabulary the at-rest audit baselines by exact class tuple). (2) The mitigation is already in the shipped block and is why the owner chose the richer form: it emits real aspect.key LEAF PATHS with site coverage, not bare aspect names, and says in terms that a listed aspect with an unlisted key renders blank and the answer is static-with-a-fallback or llm. Guidance, not enforcement, and stated as such. Its edit-1 objection (a state-mutating heal on a rejection path, the 012/056 family) is fair on process: the precedent check is now run and recorded — 012 is an improver destroying the artefact it was fixing and 056 is a regeneration dropping content, whereas this writes ONE column that is NULL, never the template, never is_active, never content_data, and is refused entirely on inactive rows.

EDITQUALITY (medium x2): (1) 'top-level prompt_template may silently mint an unused key if the real prompt is nested under workflow->steps->{step}->config'. Checked: component-creator's prompt IS top-level — jsonb_object_keys(default_config) returns [model, workflow, temperature, processing_mode, prompt_template, timeout_seconds], the generate_template step's config carries only {ai_service, input_fields}, and there is no default_config->prompts row for this agent. And this is no longer a prediction: the migration is APPLIED and the live prompt_template went 17,647 → 18,816 chars with the block present exactly once. (2) 'the WHERE clause does not pin to a single row by highest version'. The migration's first DO block does exactly that — it counts live rows and RAISEs unless the count is exactly 1, before touching anything. I believe this objection is factually mistaken about the file rather than about the risk, and I am recording that reading rather than silently ignoring it; the underlying hazard is real and is guarded.

DEBUG_HISTORIAN (medium): no pod-level deploy verification stated. Correct, and now stated as a gate on the whole verification: the Go half is INERT until a roll, so before any re-drive is credited with anything I will read the running agent-chassis pod's own build provenance and confirm e1951c24b is an ancestor of the stamped commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), per service and not per fleet, falling back to the binary probe with a present-control and an absent-control in the same exec if the startup line has scrolled. Its low objection on the verify block is answered by the file: the pre-checks, the UPDATE and the post-verify DO block are all inside one BEGIN/COMMIT, so a 0-row replace RAISEs and aborts rather than reporting success. The double-apply refusal was INDUCED after applying (re-running the file returns 'the source-vocabulary block is already present'), not asserted.

CONSTITUTION (low): the round-1 rationale was written in a hyped, ALL-CAPS register. Fair. This round is plainer.

UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1, and still the honest proportion: the class is RARE — 72 section components created since 2026-05-07 and none carries a phantom aspect at rest; 3 source-vocabulary rejections in 4 days. What changed is the CONSEQUENCE, not the rate: the birth gate went live 2026-08-18 and the first such rejection is 2026-08-21, so before the gate this output was stored and rendered silently blank and since the gate it parks the page. Arm A repairs nothing today (0 of 14 requested section types are blind; bugs_open/311's diversion closed that arm as a side effect on 08-19 and 97 of the 98 field-contract rejections predate it) and ships as prevention plus the is_active hole 311 never touched. bugs_open/345's migration 555 went live mid-build (demand-proven: 5 orchestrations carry last_error, all after 11:08:01Z, against 0 all-history), so the aspect-NAME half is now reachable reactively one wasted generation later and Arm B's unique residual is the leaf paths, the first generation saved, and the 11 items that have already spent their attempts.

plan.summary: The component writer is never shown either contract the birth gate enforces, so it complies by chance, is refused, and regenerates unchanged - 101 rejections in 8 days, 11 items parked at attempt 3, pages shipped without their tool. Make the pre-generation advisory call the GATE'S OWN code for both: resolveStorageIdentity for the field contract (so a NULL-section_type or deactivated row is no longer invisible), and LoadKnownSpecAspects/KnownAspectsSorted plus leaf-path coverage for the source vocabulary. Plus: heal a NULL section_type on the REJECTION path (is_active-gated), so the repair stops being locked behind the success it enables. Advisory throughout - every failure path degrades to today's blind generation and the gate remains the backstop.

edits.rationale: THE RISKIEST EDIT, NAMED FIRST. The regeneration UPDATE already carries this COALESCE but only runs on a SUCCESSFUL store, so a NULL section_type - which hides the row from the selector AND from the writer's advisory - can only be repaired by the success its own absence prevents. GATED ON is_active BECAUSE HEALING MAKES A COMPONENT SELECTABLE: migration 036 deactivates broken components so pages stop choosing them, and healing an inactive row here would offer a just-refused component to page planning. So it fills a metadata gap on rows already treated as live and never revives one. One column, COALESCE so an existing value is never overwritten, 'AND section_type IS NULL' so it is a no-op otherwise, best-effort so a failure cannot turn a rejection into a different error.

Arm A. Today's section_type lookup stays PRIMARY and byte-identical - it is the selector's own query (component_selector.go:183-187) and decoupling them would be a regression - and this fires ONLY on a miss, so it cannot regress a case that works today. It calls the STORE'S resolver, not a bare lookupBaseComponent, and that distinction is load-bearing: a bare by-function lookup would MANUFACTURE refusals in two live cases. On a divert-to-create there is no contract, and naming the incumbent's fields imposes a phantom one AND steers the writer to reproduce a legacy numbered-flat schema TIER D's own text calls 'the wrong shape'; on a divert-to-existing-scoped-row the real contract is the SCOPED row's schema, so naming the base row's makes the writer preserve the wrong set. Reports only when ident.IsRegeneration. Function name derived with NormaliseToKebab and requester read from the same two collected_data paths the store reads (store_generated_component_action.go:113-114), so prediction and enforcement agree by construction. Any error -> advise nothing. PRIOR-ART CHECK, NOW RUN: resolveStorageIdentity pre-exists at component_storage_identity.go:60, is unexported but in the same package `actions` so no export is needed, and was previously called from exactly ONE site (store_generated_component_action.go:115). This is therefore a NEW composition of an existing function, not an existing pattern — the librarian seat was right to want that stated rather than implied by the phrase 'the guard's own resolver'.
edits.sketch:
functionName := datahelpers.NormaliseToKebab(sectionType)
requesterSiteID := datahelpers.ExtractNestedFieldString(params.CollectedData, "input_data.site_id")
requesterDomain := datahelpers.ExtractNestedFieldString(params.CollectedData, "input_data.domain")
ident, err := resolveStorageIdentity(ctx, params.DB, functionName, requesterSiteID, requesterDomain, logger)
if err != nil { return nil, false }        // advisory: degrade to blind, never block
if !ident.IsRegeneration { return nil, false } // a create has no field contract
names := schemaFieldNamesSorted([]byte(ident.ExistingSchema))
return map[string]interface{}{"field_names": strings.Join(names, ", "), "function": ident.FunctionName, "field_count": len(names)}, true

edits.rationale: Arm B. Calls the guard's OWN LoadKnownSpecAspects and KnownAspectsSorted plus queryresolve.KnownQueryBases, so the list the refusal prints and the list the writer sees cannot drift. Rides EVERY return path including the no-component-found one, because a first-time creation invents an unresolvable source as readily as a regeneration does - the live failure WAS a diverted create; nesting it inside the found-a-row branch is the mutation the test catches. Leaf aspect.key paths carry SITE COVERAGE because the gate validates only the first segment, so bare aspect names would trade a loud refusal for a silent blank (309's damage) - the coverage number is what lets the writer decide whether a field may be required at all (cta is on 4 of 26 sites). FAILS OPEN, and independently of the field lookup: an unreadable aspect set omits the key so the prompt block stays dormant, and must NOT blank the field contract. Rejected alternative: a pure-config query_database step would be a second implementation of the gate's vocabulary in another substrate (the literal 282 anti-pattern), and the query-name half cannot be config at all since queryresolve's map is Go. WIRING, ANSWERING THE GUARDIAN'S OBJECTION WITH A READING RATHER THAN A SKETCH: these keys are NOT a new output_field and NOT new top-level fields. They are merged into the SAME map the action already returns, via a withVocabulary closure applied on all five return paths, and that map's destination is the pre-existing `output_field: existing_component`, which is already listed in generate_template's input_fields [read from the live agent_definitions row]. So migration 565's {{if .existing_component.aspect_paths}} guard resolves to this data, and the 2026-08-11 nested-field ruling's exemption applies (nested inside an already-declared object, and the seam is named in concept-register CLC-027 with its index row, shipped in the same change).

CORRECTED FROM ROUND 1, and this is the gating objection's substance. KnownAspectsSorted did NOT exist before this change: it is CREATED here by extracting the inline sort+render at component_source_guard.go:188-193, and the phantom-aspect refusal message is repointed at it in the same edit. Verified against the commit's parent rather than asserted (`git show e1951c24b~1:platform/orchestration/actions/component_source_guard.go | grep -c 'func KnownAspectsSorted'` = 0). Round 1's edit-3 rationale wrongly described it as an existing 'guard's own function' alongside LoadKnownSpecAspects — three of the four symbols this plan leans on pre-existed (resolveStorageIdentity, LoadKnownSpecAspects, KnownQueryBases); this one is extracted so it can be shared. The point of the extraction is that the list the refusal PRINTS and the list the writer SEES become one string by construction; TestKnownAspectsSorted asserts the refusal contains 'aspects that exist: ' + the advisory's own rendering, and re-inlining a separate sort in either place fails it (mutation run, not asserted).

The file had NO tests at all, which is part of how the advisory went three predicates out of step with the guard unnoticed. Eight properties, sqlmock-strict so an unexpected statement fails: section_type hit does NOT consult the resolver (reordering fails it); the blind case recovers the contract and pins the resolved function, with a mixed-case spaced input proving NormaliseToKebab; divert-to-create advises NOTHING; divert-to-scoped-row advises the SCOPED row's fields and explicitly asserts the base row's field name is absent; a resolver error never returns an error and keeps the map well-formed; the vocabulary rides even when both lookups miss; a vocabulary outage does NOT cost the field contract (the two fail-opens are independent); and the guard's message equals the advisory's rendering.

The safety property for Arm C, asserted where a caller cannot forge it: the statement must be SENT carrying 'AND is_active = true' and 'AND section_type IS NULL'. MUTATION-PROVEN, both directions, and the two tests are each other's controls: deleting the is_active condition fails both heal tests (verified by running that mutation), and deleting the whole call fails both on an unmet expectation (also verified). A third test pins that a refused CREATION sends no heal statement at all - firing one would mean writing to a component the store never identified. All three assert the refusal still happens: the heal must never rescue a write the gate refused.
edits.sketch:
mock.ExpectExec(`UPDATE content_components[\s\S]*WHERE id = \$2::uuid[\s\S]*AND is_active = true[\s\S]*AND section_type IS NULL`).
	WithArgs("test-widget", healIncumbentID).WillReturnResult(sqlmock.NewResult(0, 0))
_, err = StoreGeneratedComponentAction(context.Background(), strandingParams(db))
if err == nil { t.Fatal("a stranding regeneration must still be refused - the heal must not rescue the write") }

edits.rationale: The prompt half - the only config change, and dormant until the Go half rolls. snapshot_agent first; DO/RAISE guards on both sides (a verify block of plain SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT); anchor asserted present EXACTLY ONCE and the new block asserted absent, so a double-apply refuses. Anchor read from the LIVE prompt_template, not from the 093 on-disk snapshot, because the function-pin block proves this prompt has been edited outside the migration trail. Guarded on the RICHEST key (aspect_paths) so the block cannot half-render. The 'if it is not listed, do NOT invent a path - use static with a fallback, or llm' sentence is load-bearing, not decoration: the sibling remortgagecalculator failure wanted currency_symbol, which no site carries in any resolvable form, so a list alone would not have saved it. APPLIED 2026-08-22 and verified at the live row (block present exactly once, anchor survived, 17,647 -> 18,816 chars); the double-apply refusal was INDUCED, not asserted. The prompt is confirmed TOP-LEVEL for this agent (jsonb_object_keys(default_config) has prompt_template; the generate_template step config carries only ai_service + input_fields; no default_config->prompts row exists), answering editquality's nested-prompt objection with a reading. The first DO block RAISEs unless exactly ONE live row matches, which answers the multiple-active-rows objection. Pre-checks, UPDATE and post-verify all sit inside one BEGIN/COMMIT, so a 0-row replace aborts rather than reporting success. Numbered 565: 561 is the 345 lane's, agreed directly; 562/563/564 were taken by other lanes while the file was being written. Rollback sidecar does an exact-replace removal.

component_storage_identity.go:157-165 (the guard's own header): the is_active filter was removed on 2026-05-06 because 'with AND is_active = true a regeneration of a deactivated row fell through to the creation branch' — i.e. the gate deliberately resolves rows the advisory's is_active filter hides, which is the third divergent predicate.

Refuting my own strongest alternative [MEASURED 2026-08-22]: all 10 components carrying a field-contract refusal have 1-2 live page_components dependents, and loans-credit-health-check's dependent stores 19 content_data keys of which 12 are button_* — so the field-contract rule was protecting real stored content and the 'exact contract' rewrite would not have admitted those writes.

Rate control against overstating Arm B [MEASURED 2026-08-22]: 72 section-level components created since 2026-05-07 and NONE carries a phantom aspect at rest; the first phantom-aspect REJECTION is 2026-08-21, three days after the birth gate went live 2026-08-18. The class is rare; what changed is the consequence (silently blank -> parked page).

'last_error' is true for 5 rows, ALL created after migration 555 was applied at 11:08:01Z, against 0 in all prior history — so the reactive feedback path is live and Arm B's aspect-NAME half is now also reachable one wasted generation later.
